text:
The given figure represents two isobaric processes for the same mass of an ideal gas, then


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The two isobaric processes depicted in the figure show changes in the volume of an ideal gas with temperature under constant pressure conditions. 

Isobaric processes follow the equation $PV=nRT$, where P is pressure, V is volume, n is the number of moles of the gas, R is the ideal gas constant, and T is temperature.

When we rearrange the equation in terms of V (Volume), we get $V=\left (\frac{nR}{P}\right )T$. The slope of the volume-temperature graph in such a scenario is given by $\frac{nR}{P}$. This implies that the slope is inversely proportional to the pressure (i.e., slope $\propto \frac{1}{P}$). 

From this relationship, if one process has a higher slope compared to another, its corresponding pressure must be lower. Observing the given figure and applying this understanding, if Process 2 has a greater slope than Process 1, it indicates that $P_{2}<P_{1}$.

text: The relation between time '$t$' and distance '$x$' is $t=αx^{2}+βx$, where $α$ and $β$ are constants. The relation between acceleration $(a)$ and velocity $(v)$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The relationship between time ($t$) and distance ($x$) is given by $t=αx^{2}+βx$, where $α$ and $β$ are constants. To find the relation between acceleration ($a$) and velocity ($v$), we can follow these steps:

First, we differentiate the given equation with respect to x:

$\begin{array}{l} t=αx^{2}+βx\text{(differentiating with respect to}x\text{)} \\ \dfrac{dt}{dx}=2αx+β \\ \dfrac{1}{v}=2αx+β \end{array}$

Next, we differentiate again with respect to time to find the acceleration:

$\begin{array}{l} -\dfrac{1}{v^{2}}\dfrac{dv}{dt}=2α\dfrac{dx}{dt} \\ \text{Since}\dfrac{dx}{dt}=v,\text{we have:} \\ -\dfrac{1}{v^{2}}\dfrac{dv}{dt}=2αv \\ \dfrac{dv}{dt}=-2αv^{3} \\ \text{Therefore,}a=-2αv^{3} \end{array}$

text:
A rigid wire consists of a semicircular portion of radius $R$ and two straight sections. The wire is partially immersed in a perpendicular magnetic field $B=B_{0}\hat{k}$ as shown in figure. The magnetic force on the wire if it has a current $i$ is:


[IMG]

solution.body:
[IMG]

In a uniform field, the force on a current-carrying wire equals the force on a straight wire joining its start and end points: $⃗{F}=i⃗{L}\times ⃗{B}$.

The current enters the field going up the left straight section, goes round the semicircle and leaves going down the right section. Both ends of the immersed part lie on the field boundary, a distance $2R$ apart, so $⃗{L}=2R\hat{i}$.

$⃗{F}=i(2R\hat{i})\times (B_{0}\hat{k})=2iRB_{0}(\hat{i}\times \hat{k})=-2iB_{0}R\hat{j}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: A coin is placed on a disc. The coefficient of friction between the coin and the disc is $μ$. If the distance of the coin from the center of the disc is $r$, the maximum angular velocity which can be given to the disc, so that the coin does not slip away, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


When the coin is on the disc and the disc starts rotating, centrifugal force acts on the coin, trying to push it away from the center. The friction between the coin and the disc opposes this motion. For the coin to not slip, the frictional force must be equal to the centrifugal force acting on the coin.
The normal force (N) acting on the coin is equal to the weight of the coin, which can be represented as:
$N=mg$
where $m$ is the mass of the coin, and $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity.
The centrifugal force ($f$) that acts on the coin due to the rotation of the disc is given by:
$f=mω^{2}r$
where $ω$ is the angular velocity, and $r$ is the distance of the coin from the center of the disc.
Friction force (f) is also given by the formula:
$f=μN$
where $μ$ is the coefficient of static friction between the coin and the disc.
For the coin to not slip, the centrifugal force must be equal to the frictional force, hence:
$μmg=mω^{2}r$
Dividing both sides by $mr$, we get:
$ω=\sqrt{\frac{μg}{r}}$
This equation shows that the maximum angular velocity ($ω$) that can be given to the disc to prevent the coin from slipping off depends on the coefficient of friction ($μ$), the acceleration due to gravity ($g$), and the distance of the coin from the center ($r$).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

text: Two conductors have the same resistances at $0^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ but their temperature coefficients of resistance are $α_{1}$ and $α_{2}$. The respective temperature coefficients for their series and parallel combinations are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At $0^{\circ }\text{C}$ both resistances are $R$; for a rise $\Delta θ$, $R_{1}=R(1+α_{1}\Delta θ)$ and $R_{2}=R(1+α_{2}\Delta θ)$.

Series combination, with $R_{s}=2R$ at $0^{\circ }\text{C}$:

$R_{s}=R_{1}+R_{2}=2R\left [1+\dfrac{α_{1}+α_{2}}{2}\Delta θ\right ]\Rightarrow α_{s}=\dfrac{α_{1}+α_{2}}{2}$

Parallel combination, with $R_{p}=\dfrac{R}{2}$ at $0^{\circ }\text{C}$:

$R_{p}=\dfrac{R_{1}R_{2}}{R_{1}+R_{2}}=\dfrac{R}{2}\cdot \dfrac{(1+α_{1}\Delta θ)(1+α_{2}\Delta θ)}{1+\dfrac{α_{1}+α_{2}}{2}\Delta θ}$

Since $α\Delta θ\ll 1$, terms of second order in $\Delta θ$ are neglected and $(1+x)^{-1}\approx 1-x$:

$R_{p}\approx \dfrac{R}{2}\left [1+(α_{1}+α_{2})\Delta θ-\dfrac{α_{1}+α_{2}}{2}\Delta θ\right ]=\dfrac{R}{2}\left [1+\dfrac{α_{1}+α_{2}}{2}\Delta θ\right ]$

$α_{p}=\dfrac{α_{1}+α_{2}}{2}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

text: A small steel ball is dropped into a long cylinder containing glycerine. Which one of the following is the correct representation of the velocity time graph for the transit of the ball?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The ball, released from rest, is acted on by its weight $mg$ downward, and by the buoyant force $F$ and the viscous force $F_{v}=6πηrv$ upward.


[IMG]

$m\dfrac{dv}{dt}=mg-F-6πηrv\Rightarrow \dfrac{dv}{dt}=K_{1}-K_{2}v,K_{1}=\dfrac{mg-F}{m},K_{2}=\dfrac{6πηr}{m}$

Integrating with $v=0$ at $t=0$:

$\int\limits _{0}^{v}\dfrac{dv}{K_{1}-K_{2}v}=\int\limits _{0}^{t}dt\Rightarrow v=\dfrac{K_{1}}{K_{2}}\left (1-e^{-K_{2}t}\right )$

The velocity starts at zero, increases with ever-decreasing slope and approaches the terminal velocity $\dfrac{K_{1}}{K_{2}}$ without falling again. A straight line through the origin would need constant acceleration, which the growing viscous drag rules out.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
A force is represented by $F=ax^{2}+bt^{\frac{1}{2}}$

where $x=$ distance and $t=$ time. The dimensions of $b^{2}/a$ are:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the dimensions of $\frac{b^{2}}{a}$, let's start by identifying the dimensions of each term in the equation $F=ax^{2}+bt^{\frac{1}{2}}$, where $F$ represents force, $x$ represents distance, and $t$ represents time.

The dimension of force ($F$) is given by [MLT$^{-2}$], where $M$ is mass, $L$ is length, and $T$ is time.

The term $ax^{2}$ has the same dimension as force, so:

$[a]=\frac{[F]}{[x]^{2}}=\frac{MLT^{-2}}{L^{2}}=ML^{-1}T^{-2}$

The term $bt^{\frac{1}{2}}$ also has the same dimension as force, which gives:

$[b]=\frac{[F]}{[t]^{\dfrac{1}{2}}}=\frac{MLT^{-2}}{T^{\dfrac{1}{2}}}=MLT^{-\frac{5}{2}}$

Now, to find $\frac{b^{2}}{a}$, we substitute the dimensions of $b$ and $a$:

$\left [\frac{b^{2}}{a}\right ]=\frac{\left (M^{2}L^{2}T^{-5}\right )}{(ML^{-1}T^{-2})}=[M^{1}L^{3}T^{-3}]$

Therefore, the dimensions of $\frac{b^{2}}{a}$ are $\left [\mathrm{ML}^{3}\mathrm{T}^{-3}\right ]$, which corresponds to mass times length cubed per time cubed.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

text: In a plane EM wave, the electric field oscillates sinusoidally at a frequency of $5\times 10^{10}\mathrm{Hz}$ and an amplitude of $50\mathrm{Vm}^{-1}$. The total average energy density of the electromagnetic field of the wave is : [Use $ε_{0}=8.85\times 10^{-12}\mathrm{C}^{2}/\mathrm{Nm}^{2}$ ]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The average energy density of an electromagnetic wave is given by the formula:

$U=\frac{1}{2}ε_{0}E^{2}+\frac{1}{2}\frac{B^{2}}{μ_{0}}$

For a plane electromagnetic wave, the electric field (E) and the magnetic field (B) contribute equally to the energy density. Therefore, we can focus on just one part to find the total energy density. The formula for the energy density due to the electric field is:

$U_{E}=\frac{1}{2}ε_{0}E^{2}$

Given that the electric field amplitude ($E$) is $50\quad \mathrm{Vm}^{-1}$ and the permittivity of free space ($ε_{0}$) is $8.85\times 10^{-12}\mathrm{C}^{2}/\mathrm{Nm}^{2}$, we can calculate the energy density due to the electric field as follows:

$U_{E}=\frac{1}{2}\times 8.85\times 10^{-12}\times (50)^{2}=1.10625\times 10^{-8}\mathrm{J}/\mathrm{m}^{3}$

Since the energy density contributions from the electric and magnetic fields are equal, the total average energy density of the electromagnetic wave is just this value.

</p
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

text: A particle performs simple harmonic motion with amplitude $A$. Its speed is increased to three times at an instant when its displacement is $\frac{2A}{3}$. The new amplitude of motion is $\frac{nA}{3}$. The value of $n$ is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the new amplitude of the motion when the speed is increased to three times at a given displacement, we use the concepts of simple harmonic motion (SHM) and its formulas.
In SHM, the velocity $v$ of a particle at a displacement $x$ from the mean position can be given by the formula:
$v=ω\sqrt{A^{2}-x^{2}}$
where:
$ω$ is the angular frequency of the motion,$A$ is the amplitude, and$x$ is the displacement at that instance.Given:
Displacement at the instance, $x=\frac{2A}{3}$,Initial velocity is increased to three times at this displacement.Thus, let's find the initial velocity $v$ at $x=\frac{2A}{3}$:
$v=ω\sqrt{A^{2}-\left (\frac{2A}{3}\right )^{2}}=ω\sqrt{A^{2}-\frac{4A^{2}}{9}}=ω\sqrt{\frac{5A^{2}}{9}}=\frac{\sqrt{5}Aω}{3}$
With the velocity increased to three times, the new velocity $v^{'}$ becomes:
$v^{'}=3v=3\times \frac{\sqrt{5}Aω}{3}=\sqrt{5}Aω$
For the new amplitude $A^{'}$, the velocity $v^{'}$ at the same displacement $x$ is:
$v^{'}=ω\sqrt{A^{'}^{2}-\left (\frac{2A}{3}\right )^{2}}$
Setting the expressions for $v^{'}$ equal gives:
$\sqrt{5}Aω=ω\sqrt{A^{'}^{2}-\frac{4A^{2}}{9}}$
$\sqrt{5}A=\sqrt{A^{'}^{2}-\frac{4A^{2}}{9}}$
Solving for $A^{'}$ gives:
$A^{'}^{2}=5A^{2}+\frac{4A^{2}}{9}=\frac{45A^{2}+4A^{2}}{9}=\frac{49A^{2}}{9}$
$A^{'}=\sqrt{\frac{49A^{2}}{9}}=\frac{7A}{3}$
Therefore, the new amplitude of the motion is $\frac{7A}{3}$, which means the value of $n$ is 7.

text: Two waves of intensity ratio $1:9$ cross each other at a point. The resultant intensities at that point, when (a) Waves are incoherent is $I_{1}$ (b) Waves are coherent is $I_{2}$ and differ in phase by $60^{\circ }$. If $\frac{I_{1}}{I_{2}}=\frac{10}{x}$ then $x=$ $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For incoherent wave $\mathrm{I}_{1}=\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{A}}+\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{B}}\Rightarrow \mathrm{I}_{1}=\mathrm{I}_{0}+9\mathrm{I}_{0}$

$\mathrm{I}_{1}=10\mathrm{I}_{0}$

For coherent wave $\mathrm{I}_{2}=\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{A}}+\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{B}}+2\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{A}}\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{B}}}\cos 60^{\circ }$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{I}_{2}=\mathrm{I}_{0}+9\mathrm{I}_{0}+2\sqrt{9\mathrm{I}_{0}^{2}}\cdot \dfrac{1}{2}=13\mathrm{I}_{0} \\ \dfrac{\mathrm{I}_{1}}{\mathrm{I}_{2}}=\dfrac{10}{13} \end{array}$
